channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Animals cause nearly 1,000 train emergency stops on Kazakhstan railways
item.description: Since the start of 2026, animals on railway tracks have caused approximately 78% of emergency train stops in Kazakhstan. In the past day alone, such incidents occurred in four regions. Transport police are warning of risks to livestock and passengers, and owners are being held responsible.

item.title: UK envoy discusses Afghanistan-Pakistan tensions, supports regional peace
item.description: Richard Lindsay, the UK's Special Representative for Afghanistan, expressed concern over tensions between the Taliban and Pakistan during recent meetings in Islamabad. He stated that the UK supports efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region, following his visit to Kabul.

item.title: Chingiz Esengul uulu Appointed First Deputy Minister of Culture
item.description: Chingiz Esengul uulu has been appointed First Deputy Minister of Culture, Information, and Youth Policy. The relevant order was signed by Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. Esengul uulu previously served as Kyrgyzstan's trade representative in Turkey. He was born in 1987 and has higher education in economics and international relations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Plans Major Logistics Hub for Ozon and Alibaba Goods in Petropavl
item.description: A 102,000-square-meter logistics hub, KYZYLZHAR HUB, is planned for Petropavl, Kazakhstan, with an investment of over 29 billion tenge. The hub will store and distribute goods for online retailers like Ozon and Alibaba. An UAE investor presented the proposal, which aims to boost local businesses' shipping capabilities.

item.title: Former Head of Kazakhstan's Anti-Drug Committee Sentenced for Sexual Coercion
item.description: Daniyar Meirhan, former head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs' Committee for Combating Drug Crimes, has been sentenced in Astana. He was found guilty of coercing someone into sexual acts. The court imposed a fine of 1,500 MCI, equivalent to 6,487,500 tenge. The verdict is not yet final.

item.title: Over 1,500 Employees Dismissed in Uzbekistan Following Anti-Corruption Checks
item.description: Uzbekistan conducted 5,368 internal control checks for corruption in January-October, leading to dismissals. Checks in the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Construction, Ministry of Water Resources, Uzbekneftegaz, and Uzsuvta'minot resulted in 1,565 contract terminations. 5,000 employees faced disciplinary actions.

item.title: Former Kazakhstan Interior Ministry Drug Officer Convicted of Harassment
item.description: A former drug enforcement officer from Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs has been convicted of harassment. The details of the case and the specific charges were not provided in the initial report.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Inspects Major Mining Operation, Emphasizes Safety
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov visited the "Bolashak" mine, part of the ERG group, valued at 1 trillion tenge. He stressed the importance of industrial safety and personal responsibility of managers for employee well-being. Bektenov called for a shift from incident response to proactive risk prevention and digital control tools.

item.title: Uzbekistan IT Park Launches Remote Company Registration for Foreign Investors
item.description: IT Park Uzbekistan has introduced a "One Stop Shop" service for foreign entrepreneurs, enabling remote company registration and accelerated market entry. The service covers legal entity registration and bank account opening, with procedures completed within three days. Remote applicants need to provide a notarized power of attorney.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Co-Organize Regional Global Research Council Meeting in Seoul
item.description: Uzbekistan will participate as a co-organizer in the upcoming regional meeting of the Global Research Council (GRC) in Seoul. The Agency for Innovative Development will represent Uzbekistan, marking a significant step in strengthening the country's position in the international scientific community.

item.title: Airbus Forecasts Nearly Triple Aviation Traffic in Central Asia by 2045
item.description: Airbus predicts a nearly threefold increase in air traffic in Central Asia by 2045. The company highlights the growing importance of civil aviation, international air routes, and airport infrastructure modernization for Uzbekistan and the region's progress. Aviation plays a key role in economic development, trade, and tourism.

item.title: Turkmenistan Aims to Double SME Exports and Create 25,000 New SMEs by 2045
item.description: Turkmenistan plans to double exports from small and midsize enterprises (SMEs) and create up to 25,000 new SMEs by 2045 to diversify its economy. The strategy includes creating 50,000 jobs and increasing SME employment share to 40%.

item.title: Uzbekistan Continues to Receive Agreed Water Volume from Amu Darya Despite Rogun Dam
item.description: Uzbekistan continues to receive its agreed water volume from the Amu Darya river, despite the construction of the Rogun hydroelectric power station in Tajikistan. The dam's reservoir filling is gradual, expected to take until 2035, and the station is partially operational.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Discuss Strengthening Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held talks with Turkey's Vice President Cevdet Yilmaz. They discussed enhancing the comprehensive strategic partnership, focusing on trade, investment, industry, agriculture, construction, IT, tourism, transport, and energy. A new high-level council for business support was established, with significant agreements reached on investment projects and trade.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Qoshtepa Canal Won't Fully Utilize Amu Darya Water Until 2030, Says Minister
item.description: Uzbekistan's Water Resources Minister Shavkat Khamrayev stated that Afghanistan's Qoshtepa Canal will not begin full water withdrawal from the Amu Darya until 2030. Construction is ongoing, and Uzbekistan is in constant dialogue with Afghanistan on transboundary water resource use. While Afghanistan has a right to use Amu Darya water, the volume and terms require agreement.

item.title: Afghanistan Among Five Countries With Highest Child Casualties in Conflicts
item.description: Afghanistan is among the top five countries with the highest number of children killed or maimed in armed conflicts, according to Save the Children. Palestine, Somalia, Syria, and Yemen are also on the list. The UN verified over 171,000 such cases globally between 2005 and 2025, with over 70% in these five nations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Launches Large-Scale Business Census
item.description: Uzbekistan is commencing a comprehensive census of enterprises and entrepreneurs, covering large, medium, and small businesses, individual entrepreneurs, the self-employed, and unregistered organizations. The census will be conducted in-person and online, with results expected by September 1, 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Introduce 30-Day Visa-Free Regime
item.description: Uzbek citizens will now be able to stay in Oman for up to 30 days visa-free. An agreement signed during the Uzbek president's state visit to Oman allows visa-free entry, transit, and exit for citizens of both countries using biometric passports valid for at least six months.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Inspects Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant Construction Progress
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan visited Turkey to observe the construction of the Akkuyu Nuclear Power Plant. The visit focused on localizing the production of nuclear energy equipment and components in Uzbekistan. Discussions were held with companies involved in manufacturing and construction.

item.title: Putin, Trump, and Xi Jinping Issue Declaration on Peace
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump, and Chinese President Xi Jinping have issued a joint declaration on peace. The leaders met on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The declaration emphasizes the shared responsibility of the three nations in maintaining international peace and security and upholding the international legal order.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Budget Revenue Surpasses Plan, Indicating Economic Growth
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's republican budget revenue exceeded its plan by 27.9 billion soms in January-October 2026, with tax and customs payments up 32.3% and non-tax revenues up 50.2%. This significant increase demonstrates the effectiveness of fiscal policy and growing economic capacity, surpassing previous trillion-som milestones.

item.title: IMF Urges Kazakhstan to Raise Base Rate Amid Inflationary Pressures
item.description: The IMF has recommended Kazakhstan's National Bank raise its base rate due to persistent inflation, elevated expectations, and increased government spending pressures. Annual inflation at 9.2% is nearly double the 5% target. The IMF suggests maintaining tight monetary policy until inflation nears the target, advocating for a higher policy rate.

item.title: Student Hospitalized in Critical Condition After School Fight in Jambyl Region
item.description: A student in the Jambyl region was hospitalized in critical condition after a school fight, reportedly suffering multiple blows to the chest. Relatives claim the incident led to cardiac arrest and brain damage. The student remains in a coma.

item.title: Almaty Ambulance and Polyclinic Brigades Equipped with Smart Video Badges
item.description: In Almaty, 468 smart video badges have been issued to emergency medical service and polyclinic mobile teams. These devices record incidents, allow for distress signals, and enhance legal protection for medical workers, with footage stored for up to two years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Adopts Land-Use Plan to Protect Farmland with Compact Development
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's new land-use plan, approved by President Japarov, aims to preserve farmland by promoting compact development and earthquake-resistant housing. The strategy seeks to curb the consumption of agricultural land due to expanding single-family homes and reduce infrastructure costs. Stricter regulations will be enforced against illegal construction and unauthorized land occupation.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Prisoner Sentenced for Managing Online Drug Market from Colony
item.description: A Tashkent court has sentenced a prisoner and eight accomplices for operating an online drug market. The prisoner, serving time, coordinated drug sales via a mobile phone illegally provided by a former prison official. He received 14 years and 1 month, while others received sentences ranging from 7 to 14 years.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Outlines Priorities for University Cooperation
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev identified key areas for cooperation with foreign universities, emphasizing science and education. He highlighted water security as a critical issue for Central Asia's stability and survival, seeking collaboration with the UN University. New university campuses are planned for Astana.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kazakhmys Mines Equipped with Four New Drilling Rigs
item.description: Kazakhmys Group is upgrading its mining fleet, having delivered four new drilling rigs to its mines this year, with 21 more planned by 2027. The company is also refurbishing existing equipment, with 346 units undergoing repairs. This initiative aims to enhance production capacity and equipment reliability.

item.title: St. Petersburg Increases Migrant Work Permit Fee for 2027
item.description: St. Petersburg has approved an increase in the cost of work permits for foreign citizens starting in 2027. The fee will rise to 11,000 rubles, with some migrants paying over 15,000 rubles. A new additional tax for migrants supporting non-working family members is also planned nationwide.

item.title: Denmark ratifies security agreement with US concerning Greenland
item.description: The Danish parliament unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States concerning Greenland. The deal expands the US military role in Greenland, including permission to install the ' եւ ' missile defense system. This follows tensions after President Trump's previous threats to acquire the island.

item.title: Xi and Trump describe Shenzhen talks as positive and constructive
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump concluded their meeting in Shenzhen, describing the talks as positive and constructive. Xi stated both sides established a new format for bilateral relations: constructive relations of strategic stability. Trump affirmed the US does not support Taiwan's independence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Emergency Ministry Seeks Contractor for Kok-Art River Dam Construction
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Emergency Situations has announced a tender for the construction of a protective dam on the Kok-Art River in the Jalal-Abad region. The project, funded by the World Bank as part of the KG RESILAND initiative, is expected to take 12 months. Contractors must possess a license for hydraulic structures and submit technical and financial proposals.

item.title: International Linguaskill Exam Center Opens at Tajik University in Dushanbe
item.description: An international Linguaskill examination center, compliant with Cambridge English standards, has been established at the Tajik State University of Foreign Languages in Dushanbe. The center is equipped with modern technology for foreign language proficiency testing, aiming to enhance international language assessment systems in Tajikistan.

item.title: Olympic Champion Mikhail Shaiidorov Terminates Contract with Coach Urmanov
item.description: Olympic figure skating champion Mikhail Shaiidorov has terminated his contract with coach Alexei Urmanov. The Minister of Tourism and Sport, Yerbol Mirzakhmetov, confirmed the decision, stating it was part of Shaiidorov's preparation for the new Olympic cycle. The ministry expressed gratitude for Urmanov's three years of work and support for the athlete.

item.title: 55 Afghan Migrants Found in Hidden Truck Compartment in Turkey
item.description: Turkish police detained 55 Afghan migrants concealed in a specially constructed compartment within a truck in Diyarbakir province. Authorities have initiated deportation procedures and arrested a suspected migrant smuggler. The migrants were discovered during a highway operation targeting smuggling activities. The compartment was hidden using metal profiles and irrigation pipes.

item.title: Tajikistan's Ministry of Energy Comments on Collapse of Uzbek Power Line Support
item.description: A support tower for the 500 kV high-voltage power line L-503 collapsed in Tajikistan's Zafarabad district due to strong winds. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources stated this did not affect Tajikistan's power supply as the line is not used by its energy system. The incident caused power outages in parts of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Central Asia Learns to Discuss Superinfections with Evidence-Based Language
item.description: Central Asia is improving its capacity to discuss superinfections using evidence-based approaches. A seminar organized by the Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia (CAREC) at Nazarbayev University focused on bridging the gap between local research and international scientific discourse, particularly during the World Antimicrobial Awareness Week.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Tourism Sector Generates 303 Billion Tenge in Taxes
item.description: Kazakhstan's tourism industry has collected 303 billion tenge in taxes, representing 2.1% of the country's total tax revenue. Foreign tourists spent $1.4 billion in Kazakhstan. The sector employed over 565,000 people, contributing 6% to the national employment. Investments in tourism infrastructure saw a 68% increase.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Temporarily Withdraw 1 Million Hectares of Pastures by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to temporarily withdraw 1 million hectares of pastures from use by 2030, sow pasture grasses on 30,000 hectares, and repair over 8,000 km of pasture roads. These measures are part of a program for improving and sustainably managing pastures, according to the Ministry of Agriculture.

item.title: 131 US Lawmakers Urge Vote to Restore Afghan Protections Amid Deportation Concerns
item.description: A bipartisan group of 131 US House members is pushing for a vote to restore Temporary Protected Status for Afghan nationals, warning that deporting them to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan risks their lives. The effort aims to reinstate protections through July 1, 2029, for eligible Afghans.
